appliedOn.description: The date the distributor applied these coefficients (or the corrected date, if any of them are already active). Backdating is allowed; future dates are rejected.

coefficientIds.description: The coefficients to activate or correct, all belonging to this agreement.

currentPassword.description: The caller's current password, exactly as it was set.

Any character is accepted, including spaces and non-ASCII letters; there are no composition rules, and the value is never trimmed or transformed. closedOn.description: The date this coefficient's coverage ends (the exit case: the supply left the distribution), or the corrected date if it was already closed by an earlier call.

coefficientIds.description: The coefficients to close or correct, all belonging to this agreement.

coefficients.description: Every coefficient actually touched by this call -- the requested targets and any predecessor cascaded as a result. Empty when the whole batch was a no-op.

acceptedAt.description: When the membership was accepted. Null while it is pending: a pending membership grants no access until it is accepted. Independent of enabled.

contactEmail.description: The email address this community contacts the admin at. Null if there is none.

enabled.description: Whether the membership is enabled. A disabled one grants no access to this community, whatever its other state.

fullName.description: The admin's full name, as this community records it.

invitationExpiresAt.description: When the membership's invitation link expires. Null when it has no link that can still be used: none was sent, it was revoked or used, or it has expired.

CommunityCapabilitiesResponse.description: What the caller may do with this community.

canCreatePlants.description: Whether the caller may create plants in this community. Creating one also requires a supply the caller can see, so a true here is necessary but not sufficient for any particular supply -- SupplyCapabilitiesResponse.canCreatePlant answers that.

canDisable.description: Whether the caller may disable this community (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/disable). A platform-wide decision.

canEnable.description: Whether the caller may enable this community (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/enable). A platform-wide decision.

canInviteMembers.description: Whether the caller may send the first invitation to this community's members in bulk (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/invite). Only an active community admin of it: there is no platform-admin bypass. Whether any member is due one depends on the members' state.

canListPlants.description: Whether the caller may list this community's plants (GET /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/plants).

canListSupplies.description: Whether the caller may list this community's supplies (GET /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/supplies). A non-admin member gets only their own.

canManage.description: Whether the caller administers this community: creating and importing its supplies, reading and writing its Datadis and Shelly configuration, and triggering its synchronisation endpoints.

canManageAdmins.description: Whether the caller may invite, list, re-invite, enable and disable this community's admins (/api/v1/communities/{communityId}/admins). A platform-wide decision: being a community admin does not confer it.

canManageMembershipInvestment.description: Whether the caller may set or clear the investment recorded on this community's memberships. Only an active community admin of it: an investment is the member's own money, so there is no platform-admin bypass.

canManageMemberships.description: Whether the caller may administer this community's roster: listing, deleting and re-roling its memberships. Only an active community admin of it: there is no platform-admin bypass.

canRead.description: Whether the caller may read this community (GET /api/v1/communities/{communityId}).

canReadProduction.description: Whether the caller may read this community's communal production data. Membership, not administration: a platform admin who is not a member may not.

canRegisterMembers.description: Whether the caller may register a member in this community (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/register). Only an active community admin of it: there is no platform-admin bypass.

canUpdate.description: Whether the caller may update this community (PUT /api/v1/communities/{communityId}). A platform-wide decision: being a community admin does not confer it.

capabilities.description: What the caller may do with this community.

supplyPointCount.description: Total number of supply points in the community

password.description: The default admin's password. Between 15 and 64 characters, counting each Unicode code point as one, and no more than 72 bytes once UTF-8 encoded. personalId.description: The default admin's DNI/NIE/NIF, used as login username. It is normalised before it is stored or compared: whitespace (including the no-break space), dots and hyphens are removed and letters are upper-cased, so 12.345.678-a and 12345678A are the same identifier.

regulatoryCode.description: The identifier assigned by the regulator. In Spain this is the CAU (Codigo de Autoconsumo). It is not the provider's station code (provider_code) and not a CUPS.

installedPowerKw.description: Snapshot of the plant's installed power at authoring time, in kW

personalId.description: The DNI/NIE/NIF of the existing user who owns the supply. It is normalised before the owner is looked up: whitespace (including the no-break space), dots and hyphens are removed and letters are upper-cased, so 12.345.678-a and 12345678A are the same identifier.

coefficient.description: The coefficient value currently in force, on a 0-1 scale

sharingAgreement.description: The agreement that authored the coefficient currently in force. May be the agreement being viewed, or an earlier one.

capabilities.description: What the caller may do with their own user record.

mustChangePassword.description: Whether the caller's password was chosen by someone else and must be changed through PUT /api/v1/users/current/password. platformCapabilities.description: What the caller may do on the platform as a whole, independently of any one resource.

coefficientIds.description: The coefficients to revert to pending, all belonging to this agreement.

eurPerKWh.description: Estimated price of the energy term, in euros per kWh, before taxes. The power term, access tolls, charges, electricity tax and VAT are not included. Returned exactly as configured, without rounding.

year.description: Used only to build the generated filename ({regulatoryCode}_{year}.txt); the file content itself never encodes a year or period.

ImportMembersResponse.description: The outcome of importing a file of members.

failed.description: How many rows were not registered. Each has a code and a message in `rows`.

rows.description: One result per data row of the file, in the order of the file. Rows whose cells are all empty are skipped and have no result.

ImportMembersRowErrorResponse.description: A rule of the registration that a value of the row breaks. It names the column and the rule, never the value.

column.description: The header of the column whose value breaks the rule.

constraint.description: The rule broken: REQUIRED if a required value is empty or blank; NOT_EMPTY_ONCE_NORMALISED if the personal ID holds only whitespace, dots and hyphens; INVALID_PERSONAL_ID if the personal ID, once normalised, is not a valid DNI, NIE or NIF; MIN if the number is below `params.min`; EMAIL if the value is not an email address; NOT_AN_INTEGER if the value is not a whole number. A newer server may add rules, so a client must also handle one it does not know.

params.description: The rule's parameters, keyed in camelCase for use as i18n interpolation variables and formatted without a locale: `min` for MIN. Empty if the rule has none.

ImportMembersRowResponse.description: The result of one data row of an imported file. It carries nothing the file did not hold, and is the same whether or not the person already had an account.

code.description: Why the row failed: MEMBERSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS if the person already has a membership in this community, possibly from an earlier row of the same file; MEMBERSHIP_IMPORT_ROW_INVALID if a value breaks a rule of the registration; USER_PERSONAL_ID_INVALID if the personal ID, once normalised, is not a valid DNI, NIE or NIF; MEMBERSHIP_IMPORT_ROW_MALFORMED if the row does not have as many cells as the header. Null for a registered row.

errors.description: For MEMBERSHIP_IMPORT_ROW_INVALID, each rule broken, in the order of the columns, so that a client can write its own text; the same rules as `message`. For USER_PERSONAL_ID_INVALID, the one rule INVALID_PERSONAL_ID of the column `personalId`. Empty for any other row.

line.description: The line of the file the row starts on, the header being line 1.

message.description: Why the row failed, as a readable message in the language of the request's Accept-Language, naming the columns and rules broken but never their values. Null for a registered row.

outcome.description: REGISTERED if the member was registered, with a pending membership; FAILED if nothing was registered for this row.

token.description: The token from the invitation link: everything after the `#` of `<web client>/accept-invitation#<token>`, exactly as it appears there.

contactEmail.description: The email address this community contacts the admin at. The invitation is sent to it.

fullName.description: The admin's full name, as this community records it.

It is normalised before it is stored or compared: whitespace (including the no-break space), dots and hyphens are removed and letters are upper-cased, so 12.345.678-a and 12345678A are the same person. A value made only of those removed characters is refused.

phoneNumber.description: The admin's phone number, as this community records it. An empty or blank value is recorded as none.

email.description: The email address the invitation is sent to. An existing account keeps its own email; one without an email gets this one when the invitation is accepted.

fullName.description: The person's full name, as the invitation shows it until it is accepted. An existing account keeps its own name.

personalId.description: The person's DNI/NIE/NIF. It is normalised before it is stored or compared: whitespace (including the no-break space), dots and hyphens are removed and letters are upper-cased, so 12.345.678-a and 12345678A are the same person. A value made only of those removed characters is refused.

InvitedPlatformAdminResponse.description: A platform-admin invitation just sent, with the confirmation code generated for it.

confirmationCode.description: The confirmation code the person will need to accept: 8 characters from 0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O and U. Shown only in this response, never again by any endpoint, and never sent by email: give it to the person by another channel, such as by phone or in person.

platformAdmin.description: The invitation's row, as the list of platform admins shows it.

username.description: The user's DNI/NIE/NIF (personalId). It is normalised before the user is looked up: whitespace (including the no-break space), dots and hyphens are removed and letters are upper-cased, so 12.345.678-a and 12345678A are the same identifier.

MemberResponse.description: A member of a community: the membership, its state and the community's own member record.

acceptedAt.description: When the membership was accepted. Null while it is pending: a pending membership grants no access until it is accepted. Independent of enabled.

address.description: The member's address, as this community records it. Null if there is none.

capabilities.description: What the caller may do with this membership.

community.description: The community the membership belongs to.

contactEmail.description: The email address this community contacts the member at. Null if there is none.

fullName.description: The member's full name, as this community records it.

invitationExpiresAt.description: When the membership's invitation link expires. Null when it has no link that can still be used: none was sent, it was revoked or used, or it has expired.

invitedAt.description: When the member was last sent an invitation. Null if none has been sent.

memberNumber.description: The member's number in this community. Null if the community records none.

personalId.description: The member's DNI/NIE/NIF, normalised: the one the community registered them with.

phoneNumber.description: The member's phone number, as this community records it. Null if there is none.

user.description: The member's account, by id only: the {userId} the membership's endpoints take. Nothing else of the account is carried.

MembershipCapabilitiesResponse.description: What the caller may do with this membership.

canDelete.description: Whether the caller may remove this membership from the community.

canDisable.description: Whether the caller may disable this membership (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/{userId}/disable). Only an active admin of the community, and only on a membership with the COMMUNITY_MEMBER role. Whether it is enabled right now is the membership's enabled field.

canEditRecord.description: Whether the caller may edit this membership's member record (PUT /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/{userId}/record). Only an active admin of the community, on any membership of it whatever its role and state. Whether a change is accepted right now depends on the record sent: a membership with the COMMUNITY_ADMIN role must keep a contact email.

canEnable.description: Whether the caller may enable this membership (POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/{userId}/enable). Only an active admin of the community, and only on a membership with the COMMUNITY_MEMBER role. Whether it is disabled right now is the membership's enabled field.

canInvite.description: Whether the caller may invite this member to accept the membership, and resend or revoke its invitation. Whether one can be sent right now depends on the membership's state, its contact email and how many invitations it has been sent in the last 24 hours.

canManageInvestment.description: Whether the caller may set or clear the investment recorded on this membership.

canReadPayback.description: Whether the caller may read this membership's payback progress. Either an admin of the community, or the member themselves.

canUpdateRole.description: Whether the caller may change this membership's role.

expectedHours.description: Number of hours the period spans, times the number of supplies of the membership. A supply without any record therefore lowers coverage even when the rest are complete. Accounts for daylight saving transitions.

hoursWithData.description: Number of hourly consumption records found in the period, summed across every supply of the membership

suppliesWithData.description: Number of those supplies with at least one hourly record in the period

supplyCount.description: Number of supplies of the membership in this community

assignedProductionKWh.description: Energy assigned to every supply of the membership: selfConsumptionKWh plus surplusKWh. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals after summing, so it can differ by 0.001 from the sum of the rounded figures.

gridImportKWh.description: Energy taken from the grid by every supply of the membership over the period. Does not include self-consumed energy. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

selfConsumptionKWh.description: Energy produced by the community and consumed by every supply of the membership over the period, as reported by the distributor. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

surplusKWh.description: Energy assigned to every supply of the membership and fed back to the grid over the period. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

totalConsumptionKWh.description: Energy consumed, whatever its origin: gridImportKWh plus selfConsumptionKWh. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals after summing, so it can differ by 0.001 from the sum of the rounded figures.

coverage.description: How much of the period is backed by stored records, across every supply of the membership.

energy.description: The energy totals of every supply of the membership, summed.

period.description: The period the metrics were computed over, the same for every supply.

savings.description: What the self-consumed energy of the membership's supplies was worth over the period.

selfConsumptionRatio.description: Share of the energy assigned to the membership's supplies that they consumed rather than fed back to the grid, on a 0-1 scale, computed from the summed totals. Null when nothing was assigned to them in the period.

selfSufficiencyRatio.description: Share of the energy the membership's supplies consumed that came from the community rather than from the grid, on a 0-1 scale, computed from the summed totals. Null when nothing was consumed in the period.

amountEur.description: Estimated amount saved over the period by every supply of the membership, in euros, rounded to cents. Null only when no period could be resolved; whenever a period exists it is a figure, 0.00 when nothing was priced.

estimatedPrice.description: The estimated energy-term price, before taxes, the amount was priced with. Present only when the estimated price was used to price at least part of the period for at least one supply; null when every supply was priced with its contracted tariff, and when nothing was priced with the estimate at all.

tariffSource.description: Whether the prices behind the amount are the supplies' contracted tariffs or an estimate. A single estimated stretch of any supply makes the whole amount an estimate.

assignedProductionSampleCount.description: Number of hourly records carrying assigned production found for this hour across every supply and every day of the month. A sample count, not a day count, and independent of totalConsumptionSampleCount, since a record can carry consumption alone.

averageAssignedProductionKWh.description: Average energy assigned to every supply of the membership in this hour: self-consumed plus surplus energy. Averaged over the assigned production samples found. Null when there is no sample; 0 when there are samples and all of them are zero.

averageTotalConsumptionKWh.description: Average energy consumed by every supply of the membership in this hour, whatever its origin: grid import plus self-consumed energy. Averaged over the total consumption samples found. Null when there is no sample, never 0.

hour.description: Hour of the local day in the community's time zone, from 0 to 23

totalConsumptionSampleCount.description: Number of hourly records carrying total consumption found for this hour across every supply and every day of the month. A sample count, not a day count: on a daylight saving day one local hour holds two samples and another none.

buckets.description: Exactly 24 buckets, one per hour of the local day, ordered from hour 0 to hour 23, including the hours without any sample.

coverage.description: How much of the month is backed by stored records, across every supply of the membership, counted exactly as the aggregated energy metrics count it.

period.description: The latest published month the profile was computed over. Both bounds are null when no month could be resolved.

assignedProductionKWh.description: Energy assigned to every supply of the membership over the month: selfConsumptionKWh plus surplusKWh. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals after summing, so it can differ by 0.001 from the sum of the rounded figures.

date.description: First day of the month, a local calendar date in the community's time zone.

gridImportKWh.description: Energy taken from the grid by every supply of the membership over the month. Does not include self-consumed energy. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals. 0 when no supply stored a record.

savingsEur.description: Estimated amount the month's self-consumed energy saved across every supply that stored a record, in euros, rounded to cents. Null when no supply stored a record that month: a month with nothing stored is not a month that saved nothing. Unlike the per-supply series, which never reports null here. A supply that did store a record with no self-consumption is a measured zero and makes the amount 0.00, not null. Null exactly when tariffSource is null.

selfConsumptionKWh.description: Energy produced by the community and consumed by every supply of the membership over the month, as reported by the distributor. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

suppliesWithData.description: Number of those supplies that stored a monthly record for this month. Measured from stored monthly records, month by month, whereas the aggregated energy metrics measure their suppliesWithData from hourly records over the whole period: same name and intent, different unit, so the two figures are not comparable across endpoints. Below supplyCount, the month is incomplete.

supplyCount.description: Number of supplies the member currently owns in the community. The model records no date a supply joined, so the same count applies to every month, including months before a supply started reporting.

surplusKWh.description: Energy assigned to every supply of the membership and fed back to the grid over the month. In kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

tariffSource.description: Whether the prices behind savingsEur are the supplies' contracted tariffs or an estimate. A single estimated stretch of any supply makes the whole amount an estimate. Null exactly when savingsEur is null: with no amount there is nothing whose prices to describe.

time.description: Local time the month starts at in the community's time zone: always midnight.

estimatedPrice.description: The estimated energy-term price, before taxes, savedEur was priced with. Present only when the estimated price was used to price at least part of savedEur; null when every supply was priced with its contracted tariff, and when nothing was priced at all (no period to price, or no supplies).

estimatedRemainingMonths.description: Whole months to recover the rest at the average daily rate observed since startDate, rounded up. Zero when the investment has already been recovered. Null when no rate can be established: no investment, no savings yet, or today being startDate itself.

investmentEur.description: What the member initially contributed, in euros. Null when no investment has been recorded for this membership, which is not the same as an investment of zero.

progressRatio.description: Savings divided by investment. Not capped: a member who has recovered more than they contributed reports a value above 1. Null when either amount is null.

remainingEur.description: What is left to recover, in euros, floored at zero once the investment has been recovered. Null when either amount above is null.

savedEur.description: Estimated value of the self-consumed energy of all the member's supplies in this community since startDate, in euros. It prices the energy term before taxes only; VAT is applied only where the resolved tariff carries a rate. Null when the community has never activated a partition coefficient, so there is no period to price; zero when the period exists but the member's supplies consumed nothing from it.

startDate.description: The civil date, in the community's time zone, when the community first activated a partition coefficient and therefore began sharing energy. Null when it never has. Community-wide, not per member.

tariffSource.description: Where the prices behind savedEur came from. ESTIMATE when any part of the figure was priced from an estimated tariff rather than a contracted one, and also when no tariff was consulted at all. Never null: an amount derived from an estimate is not interchangeable with one derived from a real tariff.

acceptedAt.description: When the membership was accepted. Null while it is pending: a pending membership grants no access until it is accepted. Independent of enabled.

capabilities.description: What the caller may do with this membership.

invitationExpiresAt.description: When the membership's invitation link expires. Null when it has no link that can still be used: none was sent, it was revoked or used, or it has expired.

invitedAt.description: When the membership was last sent an invitation. Null if none has been sent.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this record was created

plant.description: Plant this coefficient belongs to. Disambiguates a supply's timeline when it participates in more than one plant.

sharingAgreement.description: Sharing agreement that authored this coefficient.

newPassword.description: The new password. Between 15 and 64 characters, counting each Unicode code point as one, and no more than 72 bytes once UTF-8 encoded. token.description: The token from the password reset link: everything after the `#` of `<web client>/reset-password#<token>`, exactly as it appears there.

personalId.description: The personal ID (DNI/NIE/NIF) of the account to recover. Spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored and letters may be in either case, as when logging in.

canManageSharingAgreements.description: Whether the caller may create a sharing agreement under this plant.

PlatformAdminInvitationResponse.description: A pending invitation to the platform-admin role.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation's current link expires. Null when it has no link that can still be used: it expired, or it was revoked, by hand or after 5 wrong confirmation codes. Resending issues a new one.

post.description:
Registers a person as an admin of the community with their DNI/NIE/NIF, full name, contact email and optional phone, and emails them an invitation to accept it at that contact email, in one operation. The membership is created pending, with the role COMMUNITY_ADMIN: it grants no access until it is accepted. The link is valid for 7 days. Only a platform admin may invite a community admin; a community admin may not.

The response is the same whether or not the person already had an account, and carries nothing from it. Inviting someone who already has a membership in this community, in any role or state, responds 409 with the `MEMBERSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS` code, and nothing is created or sent.

The DNI/NIE/NIF may be typed in any case, with spaces, dots and hyphens. Once those are removed it must be a valid DNI, NIE or NIF, with the control letter or character matching its digits; otherwise it responds 400 with the `USER_PERSONAL_ID_INVALID` code, and nothing is created or sent.

If the server cannot send emails right now (no public web URL configured, or email sending disabled), it responds 503 with the `MEMBERSHIP_INVITATION_UNAVAILABLE` code before anything is created.

Only memberships with the COMMUNITY_ADMIN role: any other is answered 404. Only a platform admin may resend them.

put.description:
This endpoint creates or replaces the configuration a community uses to connect with the
Datadis API.

The request body contains:
- **username** (required, string): Datadis user.
- **password** (optional, string): Datadis password. The password is write-only: it is
  never returned, only whether one is set (`passwordSet`).
  - Absent: the stored password is kept and the other fields are updated. If the
    community has no configuration, or its stored password is empty, the request is
    rejected with `400` and error code `DATADIS_CONFIG_PASSWORD_REQUIRED`.
  - A non-empty string: replaces the stored password.
  - `null`: rejected with `400`. The stored password cannot be cleared.
  - An empty string: rejected with `400`.
- **baseUrl** (required, string): Base URL of the Datadis API (for example
  `https://datadis.es`).

The request body does not carry `enabled`, and a body that does is rejected with `400`. This
endpoint never changes whether the Datadis integration is enabled: a new configuration starts
disabled, and an existing one keeps its current state. To switch it on or off, use
`POST .../config/datadis/enable` and `POST .../config/datadis/disable`. Enabling requires a
complete configuration.

This configuration is a mandatory step to be able to retrieve consumption data from datadis.

Authentication is mandated, utilizing an authentication token, to ensure secure access.
**Required: the caller can manage the community** (the community's `canManage` capability).

Upon successful request, the server responds with an HTTP status code of 200, along with details
about the configuration now stored.

A rejected request stores nothing and leaves any existing configuration unchanged. The server
responds with `400` when the body is invalid (a missing required field, a `null` or empty
password, a blank username, a blank or malformed base URL) or when the password is absent and
there is no stored password to keep.

post.description:
Registers each data row of a CSV file as a member of the community, as `registerMember` does: a pending membership with the role COMMUNITY_MEMBER and the row as the community's member record. Only an active community admin of the community may import members; a platform admin may not.

Nothing is sent to the members and no invitation is issued. Invite them afterwards with `sendInvitations`.

**The file.** UTF-8 or Windows-1252, the two encodings Spanish Excel saves a CSV file in ("CSV UTF-8" and "CSV"), separated by `,` or `;`, told from the header line. A file starting with a UTF-8 byte order mark is read as UTF-8; one starting with a UTF-16 byte order mark is refused; any other is read as UTF-8 if it is valid UTF-8, and as Windows-1252 otherwise. The header line names the columns, in any order: `personalId` and `fullName` are required; `memberNumber`, `contactEmail`, `address` and `phoneNumber` are optional. No other column is accepted. Each value follows the rules of the same field of `registerMember`. At most 1000 data rows; rows whose cells are all empty are skipped.

**Whole-file refusals.** If the file is neither UTF-8 nor Windows-1252, its separator cannot be told, it is not valid CSV, its header names an unknown column, a column twice or lacks a required one, or it has more than 1000 data rows, the response is 400 with a dedicated code, and nothing is registered.

**Rows.** Otherwise each row is registered in a transaction of its own, so a row that fails keeps the others. The response has one result per row. A person who already has an account is registered exactly as a new one, and their result is the same. A person who already has a membership in this community, including from an earlier row of the same file, fails with `MEMBERSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS`. Importing the same file again is therefore safe: rows already registered fail with that code, and the rest are registered.

A row whose values break rules of the registration fails with `MEMBERSHIP_IMPORT_ROW_INVALID` and lists each rule broken in `errors`, by column and constraint code, for a client to write its own text. A row whose `personalId`, once its spaces, dots and hyphens are removed and its letters upper-cased, is not a valid DNI, NIE or NIF fails with `USER_PERSONAL_ID_INVALID`, the code `registerMember` answers with, and lists the constraint `INVALID_PERSONAL_ID` of the column `personalId` in `errors`. Every `message` is in the language of the request's Accept-Language.

Registers a person as a member of the community with their DNI/NIE/NIF and the community's own member record. The membership is created pending, with the role COMMUNITY_MEMBER: it grants no access until the member accepts it. Only an active community admin of the community may register members; a platform admin may not.

get.description:
For each month of the requested period, the energy and the estimated savings of
**every** supply the member owns in this community, added up. Each energy figure
sums the unrounded per-supply monthly totals and is rounded once, to 3 decimals,
on the result; the savings are likewise summed unrounded and rounded once, to
cents. A figure can therefore differ from adding up the rounded figures of the
per-supply monthly series. Supplies in the member's other communities are not
counted.

**Source and freshness:**
Each supply's month is read from a monthly total pre-aggregated from its hourly
records. That total is rewritten once a day for every month in the Datadis sync
window (by default, the current month and the 12 before it), and on demand through
`POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/consumption/datadis/sync/monthly`. Nothing
else refreshes it: in particular, synchronising the hourly records does not. Until
the next refresh, a month can therefore lag the energy metrics, which sum the
hourly records when they are read.

**Every month is emitted:**
A bucket is returned for every month in range, in chronological order, whether or
not any supply stored a record in it, so the series has a regular time axis. This
differs from the per-supply monthly series, which omits months without a stored
record.

**Time zone and month selection:**
Months are local calendar months of the community's time zone, not UTC ones.
`startDate` and `endDate` are both required and both inclusive, and a month is in
range if and only if its local midnight on day 1 falls inside them -- the rule the
per-supply monthly series selects its pre-aggregated points by. Once in range a
month always carries its whole energy and its whole savings: bounds falling
mid-month never trim it. Pass the bounds with the zone's offset: a bound expressed
in UTC can select one month too few or too many.

**Completeness:**
`supplyCount` is the number of supplies the member **currently** owns in the
community, and `suppliesWithData` how many of them stored a monthly record that
month. A month with `suppliesWithData` below `supplyCount` is incomplete. The
model records no date a supply joined its community, so the count is the same
for every month, and the months before a supply started reporting show as
incomplete. `suppliesWithData` is measured from stored monthly records, month by
month; the aggregated energy metrics measure theirs from hourly records over the
whole period, so the two are not comparable.

**Savings:**
`savingsEur` is an **estimate** of what the month's self-consumed energy was
worth, pricing the **energy term before taxes** only, exactly as the per-supply
series does. It is `null` when no supply stored a record that month, and only
then: a month with nothing stored is a different statement from a month that
saved nothing, which reports `0.00` -- as does a month whose stored records carry
no self-consumption, a measured zero. This differs from the per-supply series,
which reports `0.00` for every bucket it emits. `tariffSource` says where the
prices came from -- `ESTIMATE` or `REAL_TARIFF` -- and a single estimated supply
makes the whole month an estimate; it is `null` exactly when `savingsEur` is.

Readable by the member themself and by community admins of this community.
Platform admins are **not** granted access on that basis alone and are answered
404, as is every other caller who may not read it, so the membership's existence
is not disclosed. A membership without supplies is answered successfully, not
with 404: every month in range, with zero totals, null savings and a
`supplyCount` of 0.

get.description:
Aggregates the consumption data stored for **every** supply the member owns in
this community into energy totals and two ratios, on a 0-1 scale. Supplies in the
member's other communities are not counted.

- `selfSufficiencyRatio`: self-consumed energy divided by total consumed energy.
- `selfConsumptionRatio`: self-consumed energy divided by the assigned energy.

Every supply is computed over the same period, exactly as the per-supply
energy-metrics endpoint computes it, and the results are added up: the energy
totals are summed across supplies and each ratio is derived **once** from those
sums, never by averaging the per-supply ratios. A ratio whose summed denominator
is zero is returned as `null`, never as `0`.

**Period:**
The period is resolved in exactly one of three ways, and the resolved bounds are
always reported in `period`, also when the caller supplied them.

- `startDate` and `endDate`: an explicit period, with the same semantics as the
  per-supply endpoint. They must be supplied together, and a `startDate` after
  the `endDate` is a bad request. **Both bounds are inclusive**: a single
  calendar day runs from `00:00` to `23:00` of that day.
- `period=LATEST_PUBLISHED_MONTH`: the most recent complete calendar month, in
  the community's time zone, that the distributor has published for any of the
  member's supplies. The distributor publishes a month's self-consumed energy
  only some days after it ends; until then the month's hourly records already
  carry consumption and the surplus the meter measured, but no self-consumed
  energy. An hourly record is therefore published when it carries self-consumed
  energy, zero included, and surplus alone does not count. A month is published
  for a supply when at least 90% of the hours it could have published carry it:
  the hours of the month from the later of its first hour and the supply's first
  published record, so a supply whose assigned production started mid-month is
  judged from that point. A month published for one supply is resolved even if
  another of the member's supplies is still unpublished. This is not necessarily
  the previous month: an unpublished or partly published month is skipped and
  the search continues backwards through the 24 complete months before the
  current one. The current month is never a candidate. When no month in the
  search window is published, no period is resolved. The period runs from
  `00:00` of the first day to `23:00` of the last day. Combining it with
  `startDate` or `endDate` is a bad request.
- Neither: from the earliest to the latest record stored for any of the member's
  supplies.

When no period can be resolved -- no published month in the search window, no
stored record at all, or no supplies to search -- the response is still
successful, with null period bounds, zero totals and null ratios.

**Coverage:**
`coverage.hoursWithData` counts the hourly records found across every supply.
`coverage.expectedHours` is the number of hours the period spans **times the
number of supplies of the membership**, so a single supply without any record
lowers coverage even when every other supply is complete. `supplyCount` and
`suppliesWithData` tell one silent supply apart from gaps spread across all of
them. Hours without a record are left out of the sums; they are never counted as
zero.

**Savings:**
`savings.amountEur` is an **estimate** of what the self-consumed energy of all
the member's supplies was worth, pricing the **energy term before taxes** only,
exactly as the per-supply endpoint does, and summed before being rounded.
It is `null` only when no period could be resolved; whenever a period exists it
is a figure, `0.00` when nothing was priced. An explicit period always resolves,
so it never yields `null`. `savings.tariffSource` is `ESTIMATE` when any part of
any supply was priced with the estimate, and `savings.estimatedPrice` then carries
the estimated price; it is `null` when every supply was priced with its contracted
tariff, and when nothing was priced with the estimate.

Readable by the member themself and by community admins of this community.
Platform admins are **not** granted access on that basis alone and are answered
404, as is every other caller who may not read it, so the membership's existence
is not disclosed. A membership without supplies is answered successfully, not
with 404.

get.description:
For each hour of the local day, the average total consumption and the average
energy assigned by **every** supply the member owns in this community, so the
member can see at which hours assigned energy goes to waste. Supplies in the
member's other communities are not counted.

- `averageTotalConsumptionKWh`: grid import plus self-consumed energy.
- `averageAssignedProductionKWh`: self-consumed plus surplus energy.

**Period:**
Always the latest published month, resolved exactly as the aggregated energy
metrics resolve `period=LATEST_PUBLISHED_MONTH`: the most recent complete calendar
month, in the community's time zone, that the distributor has published for any
of the member's supplies. An hourly record is published when it carries
self-consumed energy, zero included; surplus alone does not count, since the
distributor sends the measured surplus before it publishes the month. A month is
published for a supply when at least 90% of the hours it could have published
carry it, counted from the later of the month's first hour and the supply's first
published record. It **cannot be chosen**: only inside a published month is a
stored zero a measured zero rather than a value not published yet. The resolved
bounds are reported in `period`. When no month can be resolved -- no published
month in the search window, or no supplies to search -- the response is still
successful, with null period bounds and 24 buckets without any sample.

**Buckets:**
Always 24, ordered from hour 0 to hour 23. The hour is **local to the community**,
not UTC: each record falls in the bucket of its hour of the day in the community's
time zone.

**Averages:**
Every record of every supply and every day of the month counts as one sample of
its hour, and each average **divides by the records found**: never by the days of
the month, and never by averaging per-supply averages. Each series has its own
sample count, `totalConsumptionSampleCount` and `assignedProductionSampleCount`, and the
two can differ, since a record can carry consumption without carrying assigned
production. An average is `null` when its hour has no sample of that series, which
is never the same as `0`: an hour whose samples are all zero, such as a night hour
of assigned production, averages `0`.

**Daylight saving:**
The counts are sample counts, not day counts, and no hour is corrected. On the
October transition day the repeated local hour holds two samples of that day; on
the March transition day the skipped local hour holds none. No bucket is ever
shifted.

**Coverage:**
`coverage` is counted exactly as in the aggregated energy metrics:
`coverage.expectedHours` is the number of hours the month spans **times the number
of supplies of the membership**, so missing records -- including days of a month
published piecemeal -- show up as `hoursWithData` below `expectedHours`.
`supplyCount` and `suppliesWithData` tell one silent supply apart from gaps spread
across all of them.

404, as is every other caller who may not read it, so the membership's existence
is not disclosed. A membership without supplies is answered successfully, not
with 404.

Emails the member a new invitation link, at the contact email the community's member record has now, and stops the previous link from working, whether it was still valid, had expired or had been revoked. The new link is valid for 7 days, and `invitedAt` becomes the resend's instant. Only an active community admin of the community may resend; a platform admin may not.

A membership never invited responds 409 with the `MEMBERSHIP_NOT_INVITED` code (send its first invitation instead), one that has been accepted responds 409 with the `MEMBERSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS` code, a disabled one responds 409 with the `MEMBERSHIP_DISABLED` code, and a member record without a contact email responds 400 with the `MEMBERSHIP_WITHOUT_CONTACT_EMAIL` code.

If the server cannot send emails right now (no public web URL configured, or email sending disabled), it responds 503 with the `MEMBERSHIP_INVITATION_UNAVAILABLE` code before anything is recorded: the previous link and `invitedAt` stay as they were.

get.description:
How much of the member's recorded investment their share of the community's
energy has recovered, and roughly how long the rest would take.

`savedEur` is the estimated value of the self-consumed energy of **all** the
member's supplies in this community, from `startDate` until now, priced per
tariff segment. It prices the **energy term before taxes** only: the power term,
access tolls, charges and electricity tax are all excluded, and VAT is applied
only where the resolved tariff carries a rate. It is computed on each request and
never stored, so it reflects both new consumption and any later correction.
Supplies in the member's other communities are not counted.

`startDate` is the civil date the community first activated a partition
coefficient, and is therefore **community-wide rather than per member**. A
member who joined later has their savings divided by the community's elapsed
days rather than their own, so their apparent daily rate is lower than their
real one and `estimatedRemainingMonths` is correspondingly pessimistic. This is
a known limitation.

Null and zero mean different things throughout. A null `investmentEur` means
none has been recorded, not a contribution of zero; a null `savedEur` means the
community has never shared energy, whereas zero means it has and this member
consumed nothing from it. `estimatedRemainingMonths` is null whenever no rate
can be established, and 0 once the investment is recovered.

`progressRatio` is not capped and exceeds 1 for a member who has recovered more
than they contributed. `tariffSource` is never null and is `ESTIMATE` whenever
any part of the amount came from an estimated tariff, or when no tariff was
consulted at all.

Readable by the member themself and by community admins of this community.
Platform admins are **not** granted access on that basis alone and are answered
404, as is every other caller who may not read it, so the membership's existence
is not disclosed.

caller is not a member of it, or 403 if the caller is a member but not one of its admins.**

post.description:
This endpoint accepts the invitation of an account that has no password yet, with the token from
the emailed link `<web client>/accept-invitation#<token>` and the account's first password. It
requires no authentication, and any token presented with it is ignored.

The password must meet the same policy as a password change: between 15 and 64 characters,
counting each Unicode code point as one, and no more than 72 bytes once UTF-8 encoded.

On success the server answers 204 with no body: the token is used up, the password is set, the
membership is accepted, and, when the account had no email, the member record's contact email
becomes its email. The person is not logged in; the client must log in with the new password. A
membership that is disabled is accepted too, but grants no access until the community enables it.

An account that already has a password is answered 409 with the
`MEMBERSHIP_INVITATION_LOGIN_REQUIRED` code: the person must log in and accept with
`acceptInvitationAsCurrentUser`. A new password that breaks the policy is answered 400 with the
`USER_PASSWORD_POLICY_VIOLATION` code and a `rule` parameter. In both cases nothing changes and
the token can be used again.

A token that is unknown, malformed, expired, already used, revoked or replaced by a newer one, whose membership
has already been accepted, or whose account has been disabled, is answered 400 with the
`MEMBERSHIP_INVITATION_TOKEN_INVALID` code, the same in every case.

A platform-admin invitation, `PLATFORM` in `inspectInvitation`, also requires `confirmationCode`:
the code whoever invited gives the person by another channel. A community invitation ignores it.
On success the platform-admin role is granted as well, and, when the account had no email, the
invitation's destination email becomes its email. A missing or wrong code is answered 400 with the
`PLATFORM_ADMIN_INVITATION_CODE_INVALID` code: nothing is granted, the attempt counts against the
client address and against the invitation, and the link can be used again. The fifth missing or
wrong code on one invitation revokes its link and is answered 400 with the
`PLATFORM_ADMIN_INVITATION_CODE_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` code: the invitation must be sent again. The
code is checked after the checks above, which neither count nor use it; for a platform-admin
invitation, an account that already has a password is answered 409 with the
`PLATFORM_ADMIN_INVITATION_LOGIN_REQUIRED` code instead. A platform-admin
invitation whose account is disabled is accepted too: the role is granted, and the account still
cannot log in.

Every unusable token counts against the client address, together with failed logins, password
changes and password resets: after 20 within 15 minutes, further requests are answered 429 with a
Retry-After header until the 15 minutes that started with the first failure have passed.

This endpoint creates or replaces the configuration a plant uses to connect with a
Huawei FusionSolar Northbound API endpoint.

The request body contains:
- **username** (required, string): API user.
- **password** (optional, string): API password / system code. The password is

  - Absent: the stored password is kept and the other fields are updated. If the
    plant has no configuration, or its stored password is empty, the request is
    rejected with `400` and error code `HUAWEI_CONFIG_PASSWORD_REQUIRED`.
  - A non-empty string: replaces the stored password.
  - `null`: rejected with `400`. The stored password cannot be cleared.
  - An empty string: rejected with `400`.
- **baseUrl** (required, string): Base URL of the Huawei FusionSolar API
  (for example `https://localhost:8000/thirdData`). Mock services
  that emulate the SmartPVMS V6 Northbound Interface can be targeted by
  providing their base URL here.

The request body does not carry `enabled`, and a body that does is rejected with
`400`. This endpoint never changes whether the Huawei integration is enabled: a new
configuration starts disabled, and an existing one keeps its current state. To switch
it on or off, use `POST .../config/enable` and `POST .../config/disable`. Enabling
requires a complete configuration.

This configuration is a mandatory step to be able to retrieve the plant's production
data from the Huawei API.

Authentication is mandated, utilizing an authentication token, to ensure secure access.
**Required: the caller can manage the plant** (the plant's `canManage` capability).

Upon successful request, the server responds with an HTTP status code of 200, along with details
about the configuration now stored.

A rejected request stores nothing and leaves any existing configuration unchanged. The server
responds with `400` when the body is invalid (a missing required field, a `null` or empty
password, a blank username, a malformed base URL) or when the password is absent and there
is no stored password to keep.

get.description:
This endpoint retrieves daily consumption data from Datadis for a specific supply within a given date range.

**Authorization Rules:**
- Community Admins can retrieve consumption data for any supply they administer
- Supply owners can only retrieve consumption data for their own supplies

The consumption data includes:
- Energy taken from the grid
- Surplus energy (energy fed back to the grid)
- Self-consumption energy
- Obtain method (Real/Estimated)

Data is aggregated by day, from the hourly records, within the specified date
range. Every energy figure is in kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

**Time zone:** days follow the local calendar of the time zone the application is
configured with, not UTC. A day therefore lasts 23 hours on the spring daylight
saving transition and 25 hours on the autumn one.

**Range bounds:** `startDate` and `endDate` are both inclusive and are taken as
given, without being rounded to a day boundary. Bounds that fall in the middle of
a local day produce a partial first and last bucket, so a caller wanting whole
local days must pass them at local midnight and at 23:59:59 local time, offset
included -- for example `2023-04-01T00:00:00+02:00` to
`2023-04-30T23:59:59+02:00` for April 2023 in Europe/Madrid. A day with no stored
record is returned with zero energy rather than omitted.

Each day is priced over its own local day, clipped to the requested bounds, so a
partial edge bucket's savings cover exactly the hours its energy fields cover.

**Savings:** `savingsEur` is an **estimate** of what the bucket's self-consumed
energy was worth. It prices the **energy term before taxes** only: the power
term, access tolls, charges and electricity tax are all excluded, and VAT is
applied only where the resolved tariff carries a rate. `tariffSource` says where
the prices came from -- `ESTIMATE` for a computed approximation, `REAL_TARIFF`
for the supply's contracted tariff -- and a single estimated stretch of the
bucket makes the whole amount an estimate. A bucket with no self-consumption,
and a bucket with no stored record at all, reports `0.00`.

Datadis publishes a month's self-consumption around the 10th of the following
month, so the current month has no self-consumption data yet and its savings
come back as zero.

This endpoint retrieves monthly consumption data from Datadis for a specific supply within a given date range.

**Authorization Rules:**
- Community Admins can retrieve consumption data for any supply they administer
- Supply owners can only retrieve consumption data for their own supplies

The consumption data includes:
- Energy taken from the grid
- Surplus energy (energy fed back to the grid)
- Self-consumption energy
- Obtain method (Real/Estimated)

Data is aggregated by month within the specified date range. Every energy figure
is in kWh, rounded to 3 decimals.

**Source and freshness:** each month is read from a monthly total pre-aggregated
from the supply's hourly records. That total is rewritten once a day for every
month in the Datadis sync window (by default, the current month and the 12 before
it), and on demand through
`POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/consumption/datadis/sync/monthly`. Nothing
else refreshes it: in particular, synchronising the hourly records does not. Until
the next refresh, a month can therefore lag the energy metrics, which sum the
hourly records when they are read.

**Time zone:** each month covers the local calendar month of the time zone the
application is configured with, not the UTC one, so its total includes the first
and last local hours of the month and nothing from its neighbours.

select the months intended: local `2023-01-01T00:00:00+01:00` is
`2022-12-31T23:00:00Z`, so a bound expressed in UTC can select one month too few
or too many.

falls inside the inclusive bounds, and once included it always carries the whole
month's energy and the whole month's savings -- bounds falling mid-month never
trim it. A request ending on the 15th therefore still returns that month in
full.

the prices came from -- `ESTIMATE` for a computed approximation, `REAL_TARIFF`

get.description:
This endpoint aggregates the consumption data stored for a specific supply into energy
totals and two ratios, on a 0-1 scale:

- `selfSufficiencyRatio`: self-consumed energy divided by total consumed energy.
- `selfConsumptionRatio`: self-consumed energy divided by the energy assigned to the supply.

Both ratios are computed by summing every record first and dividing once, so hours of
different magnitude weigh differently. A ratio whose denominator is zero is returned as
`null`, never as `0`.

**Authorization Rules:**
- Community Admins can retrieve energy metrics for any supply they administer
- Supply owners can only retrieve energy metrics for their own supplies

**Period:**
`startDate` and `endDate` are optional and must be supplied together; supplying exactly
one of them is a bad request, as is a `startDate` after the `endDate`. When neither is
supplied the period spans from the supply's earliest stored record to its latest, and a
supply with no record at all returns a successful response with null period bounds, zero
totals and null ratios.

**Both bounds are inclusive.** A caller wanting a single calendar day must pass `00:00`
to `23:00` of that day, not `00:00` to the following `00:00`, which would count the
boundary hour in both days.

The `coverage` object reports how many hourly records were found against how many hours
the period spans, so a partially synchronised period can be told apart from a genuinely
low ratio. Hours without a record are left out of the sums; they are never counted as
zero.

**Savings:**
`savings.amountEur` is an **estimate** of what the self-consumed energy of the period
was worth. It prices the **energy term before taxes** only: the power term, access
tolls, charges and electricity tax are all excluded, and VAT is applied only where the
resolved tariff carries a rate. `savings.tariffSource` says where the prices came from
-- `ESTIMATE` for a computed approximation, `REAL_TARIFF` for the supply's contracted
tariff -- and a single estimated stretch of the period makes the whole amount an
estimate.

The amount **does not distinguish missing data from genuine zeros**: an hour with no
stored record contributes nothing, exactly as it contributes nothing to the energy
totals, so a partially synchronised period yields a proportionally low figure rather
than a flagged one. `coverage` is the field that tells the two apart. Consistently
with that, an explicitly requested period containing no record at all is worth `0.00`,
while `null` is reserved for the one case where no period could be resolved: a supply
with no stored record and no requested period.

This endpoint accepts an invitation of one of the caller's own memberships, with the token from
the emailed link `<web client>/accept-invitation#<token>`. It is the way to accept for an account
that already has a password; the password is neither read nor changed.

On success the server answers 204 with no body: the token is used up and the membership is
accepted. The client should then read the current user again to see the new membership. A
membership that is disabled is accepted too, but grants no access until the community enables it.

A token of another account's membership is answered like any unusable token.
A token that is unknown, malformed, expired, already used, revoked or replaced by a newer one, whose membership
has already been accepted, or whose account has been disabled, is answered 400 with the
`MEMBERSHIP_INVITATION_TOKEN_INVALID` code, the same in every case.

A caller who must change their password is answered 403 with the `USER_PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`
code before the token is looked at; the link stays usable once the password has been changed.

A platform-admin invitation, `PLATFORM` in `inspectInvitation`, also requires `confirmationCode`:
the code whoever invited gives the person by another channel. A community invitation ignores it.
On success the platform-admin role is granted, and, when the account had no email, the
invitation's destination email becomes its email. A missing or wrong code is answered 400 with the
`PLATFORM_ADMIN_INVITATION_CODE_INVALID` code: nothing is granted, the attempt counts against the
client address and against the invitation, and the link can be used again. The fifth missing or
wrong code on one invitation revokes its link and is answered 400 with the
`PLATFORM_ADMIN_INVITATION_CODE_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` code: the invitation must be sent again.

Every unusable token counts against the client address, together with failed logins, password
changes and password resets: after 20 within 15 minutes, further requests are answered 429 with a

This endpoint lets the authenticated user replace their own password. It always acts on the
caller, so it cannot be used to change anybody else's password.

The current password must be supplied and must match. The new password must be between 15 and
64 characters long, counting each Unicode code point as one, and no more than 72 bytes once
UTF-8 encoded. Any character is accepted, including spaces and non-ASCII letters; there are no
composition rules, and the value is never trimmed or transformed. The new password must differ
from the current one; the comparison is exact, so a value that differs only by case or by leading
or trailing spaces is a different password.

On success the server answers 204, clears the "must change password" flag and ends every
session opened with the previous password: every token issued before the change, including the
one used for this request, is rejected with 401 from then on, and the access cookie is removed.
The client must log in again with the new password.

A wrong current password is answered 400 with the `USER_CURRENT_PASSWORD_INCORRECT` code, never
401, and changes nothing. A new password that breaks the policy is answered 400 with the
`USER_PASSWORD_POLICY_VIOLATION` code and a `rule` parameter naming the rule that failed:
`TOO_SHORT`, `TOO_LONG` or `TOO_MANY_BYTES`. A correct current password with a new password
exactly equal to it is answered 400 with the `USER_PASSWORD_UNCHANGED` code: nothing is changed,
the caller's token stays valid and the "must change password" flag stays as it was. A wrong
current password is reported as such, whatever the new password.

Neither an unchanged password nor a policy violation counts as a failed attempt. Wrong current
passwords count together with failed logins on the same account. After 5 failures
on the account, or 20 from the same client address, within 15 minutes, further changes are
answered 429 with a Retry-After header, without checking the current password and without
affecting the caller's token, until the 15 minutes that started with the first failure have
passed.

put.description:
This endpoint lets the authenticated user change how the community reaches them: email,
postal address and phone number. It always acts on the caller — there is no
user identifier to supply — so it cannot be used to edit anybody else.

Name, DNI and member number are not editable here: they identify the member to the
community and to the distributor. A community keeps its own name and member number for
the member on the membership's member record.

Omitting `email`, `address` or `phoneNumber` clears the stored value. An empty or blank
`email` also clears it; any other value must be a valid email address.

**Required: any authenticated user (edits their own contact details).**

delete.description:
This endpoint enables the removal of a user from the system by specifying the user's unique identifier within the endpoint path.

    To utilize this endpoint, clients send a DELETE request with the targeted user's ID, requiring authentication for secure access.
    **Required: nobody may use it on another user's account, and you cannot delete your own account.** Nobody may delete another user's account: neither a Community Admin, whatever their role in the user's communities (#415), nor a Platform Admin (#446). A caller who cannot see the user is answered 404; one who can is answered 403.

    The account is shared by every community the person belongs to (#415). To remove a member from one community, delete their membership instead (`DELETE /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/{userId}`); to suspend them, disable it (`POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/memberships/{userId}/disable`).

    Deleting the account also deletes every membership of the user, in every community, with its member record, and every token of the user. Memberships the user invited are kept, with no inviter, and sharing agreements and distributor files the user created, edited or uploaded are kept, with no creator, editor or uploader.

    The account of a user who owns supplies, in any community, is not deleted: the request is answered 409 with `USER_OWNS_SUPPLIES`, and nothing is deleted. To stop their access, disable the account instead (`POST /api/v1/users/{userId}/disable`); to delete it, delete their supplies first (`DELETE /api/v1/supplies/{supplyId}`). The last enabled platform admin is not deleted either (409 `USER_LAST_PLATFORM_ADMIN`).

    Upon successful deletion, the server responds with an HTTP status code of 200, indicating that the user has been successfully removed.

    In cases where the deletion process encounters errors, the server returns an appropriate error status code, along with a descriptive error message to guide clients in diagnosing and addressing the issue.

post.description:
This endpoint removes platform-administrator privileges from the user identified in the endpoint path.

Proper authentication, through an authentication token, is required for secure access.
**Required: Platform Admin. You cannot revoke your own privileges.**

Once the caller is allowed, the target is checked: an unknown user answers 404, and a user who is not a platform admin answers 409 USER_NOT_PLATFORM_ADMIN.

Two safety rails apply: a platform admin cannot revoke their own privileges, and the system can never be left without an enabled platform admin. Revoking the last enabled platform admin answers 409 USER_LAST_PLATFORM_ADMIN; since the caller is themselves an enabled platform admin, this can only happen when two revokes run at the same time. Revoking a disabled platform admin is always allowed, since it leaves the number of enabled platform admins as it is.

Upon a successful request, the server responds with an HTTP status code of 200, indicating that the user is no longer a platform administrator.

In situations where the operation encounters errors, the server responds with an appropriate error status code, accompanied by a descriptive error message to assist clients in diagnosing and resolving the issue.

get.description:
This endpoint retrieves all supplies associated with a specific user by their unique identifier.

**Authorization Rules:**
- Community Admins (of the target user's community) can retrieve supplies for that user
- A user can retrieve their own supplies
- Being a Platform Admin is **not** sufficient (#446): a Platform Admin who administers none of
  the user's communities cannot see the user, and is answered 404

**What the listing contains:** only the supplies the caller may read one by one
(`GET /api/v1/supplies/{supplyId}`) — all of them for the user themselves, otherwise only
those in the communities the caller administers.

Authentication is required using a Bearer token.
